name: sgs/decorative-image
title: Floating layer
description: Floats an image, text, a label or a badge over its section at a set position, size and angle.

sgs._comment_mediaElements: Adopts object-fit, focal-point and overlay only, unprefixed (one media slot). box-shape is NOT adopted as an atom: its Width, WidthUnit, Height and border bases are this block's own width, height and border attributes, so the atom would put --sgs-media-width and a second border on the inner image of every wrapper layer and add second Width, Height and border rows. The layer takes the atom's SHAPE only: the block-private `shape` attribute uses the atom's vocabulary and clip-path map (box-shape.js::validateShape, sgs_media_atom_box_shape_clip_paths) and clips the layer root. The layer paints its own box (border, radius, fill, shadow, height) on its root through the block-private attributes below, built from the shared border, shadow and fill assemblers (sgs_border_element_decls, sgs_shadow_decls, sgs_background_paint_decl), the way sgs/before-after does for its frame.

fx._comment_motionSurface: Spec 38 §2, MotionPath row: 'Exposure surface: Inspector on `sgs/decorative-image`' — cited by name as that effect's primary target, and §10's reduced-motion table separately names this block's existing reduced-motion arm as the reference implementation MotionPath's own Suppress behaviour matches. This block has no text/section/svg/svg-subtree/track/item-set signal of its own (it renders a raster or video, absolutely positioned — no RichText, no containerKind, no bgSvgContent, no scrollable overflow, no filter pairing), so `generate-fx-qualifying-blocks.py`'s normal requires-based route resolves zero provisions for it. `motion-path`/`scrub` both have `requires='none'` (broadly available wherever a panel already exists) but cannot, by themselves, CREATE a panel anywhere — that rule is what stops every sgs/* block acquiring a panel from `scrub` alone. This flag is the block's own declaration that it is a legitimate host regardless, read by `_block_provisions()` alongside `draggable`/`pairedFilter` and satisfying the panel gate the same way a real requires-match would. Mirrors `providesNatively` above (a fact the block owns) for the opposite direction: that excludes an effect this block already has natively; this includes a block that has no requires-derivable structural provision but is still spec-named as a legitimate fx target.

image.label: Image
image._note: An empty-string prefix does NOT trigger the default-convention resolver (it's checked with `if (element.prefix)`, and '' is falsy) — so opacity/zIndex are mapped explicitly rather than relying on bare-attribute matching. positionX/positionY are the centre model (a percentage of the section with a centring translate), not CSS offsets, so they stay unmapped; css:top/right/bottom/left map to the edge offsets positionTop/Right/Bottom/Left, which anchor their axis to its edges (includes/helpers-layer-edges.php). No layer field is declared (this is not a composite). The old motion cluster (transition-duration/transition-timing-function) is still deliberately NOT declared here — these are JS-driven scroll-triggered parameters, not CSS transitions, and mapping them there would misrepresent the mechanism.

attributes._comment_decorMedia: Migrated 2026-05-05 — legacy imageId/imageUrl/imageAlt retained for deprecation. New instances should use decorMedia (unified image-or-video slot).
attributes._comment_artDirection: Art-direction tiers (2026-08-07) — same {base}/{base}Tablet/{base}Mobile shape and ID-wins-URL-falls-back pairing as sgs/media and sgs/hero, so a client meets ONE interaction for 'a different crop on narrow screens' wherever images appear. A tier left empty falls back to the desktop image at that width (degrade to MORE content, never less). Image-only: the decorMedia video branch returns before the tier siblings are built.

imageDecorative._comment: Spec 35 item 18 / {element}Decorative convention (matches sgs/media's imageDecorative). Default true because a floating image is decoration by default. It governs only the (alt empty plus aria-hidden when on, imageAlt when off); text and blocks inside the layer are always read out.

attributes._comment_edges: Edge offsets, per device: a length from the shared length control, negative values included. An axis whose edge (left or right; top or bottom) holds a value at any device is placed by its edges at every device and drops its centre percentage and its half of the centring translate; an axis with none keeps positionX/positionY. Unset prints nothing.
attributes._comment_width: Width per device: a length from the shared length control (px, %, em, rem, vw) or max-content (Fit the content: the layer sizes to its content, capped at the parent unless maxWidth is set). A narrower device inherits the wider one's value.
attributes._comment_maxWidth: The layer's widest size per device: any length the shared length control stores (px, %, em, rem, vw) or none. Unset prints no cap (CSS's own initial value), so a fixed width holds at every device unless the client limits it; Fit the content keeps its max-width:100% until a value is set.
attributes._comment_shape: Named shape on the layer root, the vocabulary sgs/media offers (box-shape atom): none, rounded, circle, square. Prints clip-path only; unset prints nothing. A shape alone draws nothing: an empty layer still needs a border, a fill or a shadow.
attributes._comment_box: The box the layer paints on its own root, so an empty layer can draw a ring, a disc or a tinted panel. Every attribute prints nothing while unset. A layer with no media and no content renders only when a border width, a gradient ring, a shadow or a fill is set.
